newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MPC 9-mth net up due to telecoms, property.
newsitem.headline: MPC 9-mth net up due to telecoms, property.

text.p: Diversified conglomerate Metro Pacific Corp said on Thursday its nine-month earnings were boosted by investments in telecommunications and property.

It also generated other income, at a net of 339 million pesos, from the sale of part of its convertible bonds in Smart Communications Inc which was offset by non-recurring charges taken by Steniel Manufacturing Corp, its packaging business.

Metro Pacific reported after-tax profit in the January to September period jumped by 93 percent to 590.528 million pesos from 305.238 million pesos in the year-earlier period despite the difficulties it experienced in the packaging business.
Sales increased by 6.0 percent to 3.962 billion pesos in the first three quarters from 3.755 billion pesos last year.

"This performance is the result of our strategy of investing for the long term in four core businesses rather than being dependent on a single industry," Metro Pacific president Napoleon Nazareno said in a statement.
"This strategy has enabled us to be resilient to downturns in particular industries, while taking advantage of opportunities in a changing and dynamic market," he added.
The four core businesses are banking, telecommunications, property and consumer products.

In the real estate sector, Metro Pacific said it has entered into firm contracts this month to sell 16 hectares of land in the Fort Bonifacio area with a total sales value of about 28 billion pesos with third parties and shareholders of Fort Bonifacio Development Corp (FBDC).
FBDC is a joint venture between a Metro Pacific-led consortium and the government that will develop the 214-hectare former Fort Bonifacio military base on the edge of the Makati financial district.
Smart, Metro's telecommunications affiliate, now has an average revenue per subscriber per month of 1,000 pesos. It currently has a subscriber base in excess of 260,000, the company said.
